pr_title: Add notification policies and notification requests
pr_body:
Allow users to set a policy for who they want to see notifications from. The rest appear as notification requests that can be perused and accepted separately.

Instead of silently dropping messages from limited accounts, filter them and allow users to peruse them as notification requests, even if the user has no policy to filter notifications set.

REST API:

- `GET /api/v1/notifications/requests`
- `POST /api/v1/notifications/requests/:id/accept`
- `Post /api/v1/notifications/requests/:id/dismiss`
- `GET|PUT /api/v1/notifications/policy`

___

Fixes MAS-39, fixes #12181, fixes #28429, fixes #24117

issue_context.title: Notifications from limited accounts do not arrive for admins/mods
issue_context.body:
### Steps to reproduce the problem

1. Have a local user limited
2. The local user sends a DM or message to an admin or mod who does not follow them 
3. The admin/mod does not receive notification of the message


### Expected behaviour

A user who is limited should still notify admins/mods when they message

### Actual behaviour

DMs are sent by limited user, but admin/mod does not get notified, so it looks as if they are ignored

### Detailed description

It makes sense that if a user is limited, others who do not follow them will not get notified when they message, either publicly or via DM.

However we have had issues with users DMing an admin or moderator, and not having a response because while the messages are sent, the recipients are not notified.

While admins/mods may not necessarily want every message from limited users, it has led to further interpersonal issues, as the user understandably feels that they have been ignored. In my case I would have responded to the user when I got their message, but I was not notified of any of their messages.

I am suggesting that an option exist for a capability that can be added to user roles that allows you to bypass the limit feature, and receive messages from limited users. This would allow mods and admins, or any other user role created, to opt-in to letting limited users message them for moderation purposes.

### Specifications

Mastodon v4.1
comments: I suggest a specific toggle in the admin interface for "have limit users be able to direct-message people with the role <X>", or have the Direct Messages interface also list limited users, in a manner similar to how other platforms to "Message Requests"

review_comments: I see how it's being used - but does the `requires_new_policy` here capture something that `changed?` doesn't capture?
If the policy is newly initialized, then `changed?` is true even if we didn't change anything.

Ah I see - if it comes from a pure `NotificationPolicy.new` then `changed?` is false to start with, but once we add the account (either by setting, or via `build_*` as done here) then it's already dirty so we need the more specific check on the fields we care about. Given that, fine as-is.

I guess if we really wanted to kill the local var you could do something with `policy.changed` down here and see if any of the relevant attributes are in there.

We probably want an index on `account_id, id` with a `WHERE dismissed = false` or something similar since the two most frequent queries will be to search for non-dismissed requests for an account, sometimes ordered and paginated by `id`.
The notification count stuff (and maybe the caching?) should have some coverage.

The `summarize!` method in this class is interesting enough that it should have coverage.
This is only updated when notifications are created, not when they are deleted, which means the counts can get inaccurate or people can end up with “ghost” notification requests.

Are there scenarios where any accounts will already have a policy? Assuming these migrations are run close together, it seems unlikely ... curious if I'm missing something obvious or if we're just being defensive here for the edge case where migrations are run w/out downtime and an account could hypothetically create a policy between the migrations running...
Yes, this is programmed defensively because there are situations when admins forget to run migrations.
Could the read replica be set in an `around_action`?
I'm trying to be consistent with the style proposed by @krainboltgreene originally. Be very explicit where read-replicas are used.

Cool, makes sense. I guess if at some point that pattern becomes less one-off here and there and more widespread, we could reconsider that.

Separately, while working on a serializer performance branch, I noticed a sort of mix of styles around how the `relationships` are passed into serializers. This PR is open to standardize them - https://github.com/mastodon/mastodon/pull/29033/files - that could apply here as well (leave the `@requests` assignment in the action wrapped in with_read_replica, but move the relationships presenter wrapping to a private method). All of that is in service of reducing diff size on eventual serializer perf PR ... so not critical, but will make it easier.
Is it possible to create the column this way in the initial migration ... or does it need to be a follow-up alter?

Don't think there's a way to make it part of `create_table`, but maybe it could be part of the same migration. Either way, I'm doing it the same way all previous migrations of this type have been done and don't see any downside to it.
I think, for existing users, we should be backfilling these with the current `interactions.must_be_following` and `interactions.must_be_following_dm` to not break people's expectations.
